title: Anthropic grants outside evaluator METR employee-level access in AI safety push
key_facts: Anthropic gives six researchers from METR, a nonprofit that tests frontier AI models, employee-level access to assess its models, safety practices and risk management
Announced in an Anthropic blog post on Thursday 15 Oct 2026
METR gets company laptops, office space and internal tools roughly on par with Anthropic's own risk assessment teams
METR will publish its own assessments; Anthropic cannot veto publication but can require redaction of narrow categories (customer data, privileged material, model architecture details)
METR is the only evaluator so far in the top tier of a three-tier system Anthropic is building; SecureBio sits in the bottom tier and needs approval to publish
Follows a September essay by CEO Dario Amodei proposing outside evaluators inside AI labs; OpenAI pledged the same
Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Nvidia and xAI have signed a White House accord committing to independent review
quote_evidence: Anthropic is giving employee-level access to six researchers from METR, a nonprofit that tests frontier AI models, to independently assess Anthropic's models, safety practices, and risk management, the company said in a blog post on Thursday.
Anthropic can't veto publication, but we can require them to redact information if it falls into narrow, pre-defined categories
why_it_matters_hint: Outside checkers can now see inside a leading AI lab and publish what they find, which tests whether labs can be held accountable.
notes: Read at TechCrunch (Reuters link returned 401). TechCrunch relays Anthropic's own blog post.
